title: FLAG: An FPGA-Based System for Low-Latency GNN Inference Service Using Vector Quantization
problem: Real-time GNN inference serving faces two bottlenecks: intensive preparation (neighbor aggregation, feature computation) and the neighborhood explosion problem (exponential neighbor set growth across layers), making it difficult to meet low end-to-end latency service level agreements.
motivation: GNN inference serving is critical for real-time recommendation and knowledge graph applications; current systems cannot meet latency SLAs due to preparation overhead and neighborhood complexity.
method: FLAG addresses latency by moving heavy work offline. It precomputes the neural network's intermediate results (embeddings) and compresses them using vector quantization (storing full vectors as indices into a small lookup table, reducing memory and computation). At serving time, an FPGA accelerator loads these compressed embeddings and quickly combines neighbor information without expensive recalculations. This eliminates the bottleneck that happens when computation is done live for each query.
key_novelty: Precomputing compressed embeddings offline via vector quantization enables an FPGA to efficiently serve graph neural network predictions without hitting the exponential neighbor-growth bottleneck.
contributions: Offline preprocessing strategy with vector quantization for embedding compression
FPGA accelerator design for lightweight GNN aggregation
Elimination of neighborhood explosion overhead via precomputation
primary_theme: FPGA-accelerated GNN inference with vector-quantized embeddings
